text:
Squander Early Rally Effort 07-Dec-18 12:55 ET Dow -425.66 at 24522.01, Nasdaq -161.74 at 7026.52, S&P -47.20 at 2648.75
[BRIEFING.COM] The S&P 500 trades near session lows with a loss of 1.9% after being up as much as 0.5% shortly after the start of trading. The Dow Jones Industrial Average is down 1.8% after being up as much as 0.5%, and the Nasdaq Composite is down 2.4% after being up as much as 0.2%.
The inability to sustain an early rally effort following yesterday's strong rebound, and a generally supportive employment report, has raised some concern that this week's down leg has yet to run its course. Volatile price action has
Continued trade headline volatility has also caused some annoyance for investors.
President Trump rehashed that talks with China are "going very well," though trade adviser Peter Navarro, a well-known China hawk, reminded everyone about the increase in the tariff rate that will happen if trade talks are not resolved in the 90-day window.
Underperforming the broader market today are the information technology (-2.9%), health care (-2.6%), consumer discretionary (-2.6%), and industrial (-2.2%) sectors.
Most components are down within the heavily-weighted tech group despite Broadcom (AVGO 228.29, +1.05, +0.4%) giving the group a reason to rally with its upbeat earnings report and outlook. The non-response has been construed as a negative signal that sector selling efforts may not have run their course yet. The sector has lost nearly 14.0% this quarter.
Tech heavyweights Apple (AAPL 170.23, -4.49, -2.6%) and Microsoft (MSFT 106.04, -3.13, -2.9%) have been influential drags on the sector. Apple in particular remains
Notable laggards have also included the cyclical transport and chip stocks. The Dow Jones Transportation Average is down 2.9%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is down 2.7%. American Airlines (AAL 33.80, -3.14, -8.5%) and NVIDIA (NVDA 147.71, -10.60, -6.6%) have dragged on their respective groups.
Conversely, the energy (+0.6%) and utility (+0.6%) sectors are the only groups in the green today.
Looking at energy, OPEC and certain non-OPEC producers (Russia importantly) announced an agreement to cut oil production by 1.2 million barrels per day. Iran will reportedly be exempt from the production cut requirement after requesting exception due to U.S. energy sanctions already hurting Tehran. WTI crude has jumped 4.4% to $53.72/bbl on the agreement, elevating the oil-sensitive energy sector.
In other corporate news, lululemon athletica (LULU 118.35, -13.05) and Ulta Beauty (ULTA 258.09, -34.85) have dropped 10.0% and 11.8%, is down despite beating top and bottom line estimates, while Ulta issued Q4 guidance below consensus.
U.S. Treasuries are mixed with the shorter-term securities on the rise. The 2-yr yield is down four basis points to 2.73%, and the 10-yr yield is up one basis point to 2.88%. Meanwhile, the U.S. Dollar Index is down 0.1% to 96.71.
